title: Back Pain
hpi_narrative: {{patient_name}} presents with acute low back pain radiating down the leg (sciatica) following lifting/twisting injury. Pain follows dermatomal distribution — most commonly L4-L5 or L5-S1. Exam: positive straight leg raise test (pain <70° elevation). Neurologic exam to identify affected root: L4 (patellar reflex, medial leg), L5 (foot drop, great toe dorsiflexion, dorsal foot), S1 (Achilles reflex, plantar flexion, lateral foot). Cauda equina RED FLAGS: bilateral sciatica, saddle anesthesia, urinary retention/incontinence, fecal incontinence — surgical emergency. Conservative management for uncomplicated herniation: NSAIDs, physical therapy, continue activity as tolerated (bed rest NOT recommended). Most resolve in 6 weeks. MRI if not improving or neurologic deficit (not urgent CT/bone scan — but MRI is gold standard). Epidural steroid injection for radicular pain. Surgery (microdiscectomy) if severe deficit, cauda equina, or failed 6+ weeks conservative.
